judgementOnFix04sCauseNumberReasoning.andICorrectMyOwnPriorRow: My last row asserted that 'FB is bound inside this repository to Class B'. judgementOnFix04sCauseNumberReasoning.andICorrectMyOwnPriorRow: My last row asserted that 'FB is bound inside this repository to Class B'. defectsNoCounterCanSee.title: The central raster must be taken WITH annotations, and the reason is stronger than the net pixel count suggests - but a with-annotations raster of these forms shows the issuer's own table rules broken.

Not because 1,591 pixels would otherwise vanish, but because the with-annotations raster is byte-faithful to the issuer's own document at 300 dpi while the hide-annotations raster is a page that exists nowhere - neither the issuer's file nor what the participant sees on screen. A visual reviewer should be told in advance that the broken column rules are the issuer's, or they will file them as a build defect.

defectsNoCounterCanSee.title: One key name carries two different definitions inside one report file.

Those two keys are neighbours in scripts/rcap-official-forms/rcap-output-glyph-reading.mjs, where addedGlyphsReadFromOutputBytes is defined as 'every glyph any flattened widget appearance in the output draws' - which, with zero flattened appearances, would have to be 0.
defectsNoCounterCanSee.whyItIsNotAContradiction: FIX04 took only the flattened-appearance count from that module; the Indiana builders compute the other key themselves and mean something else by it. I confirmed what they mean: 607 + 1,010 = 1,617, which is exactly the non-whitespace glyph count of the 48 declared write values I summed from the same file. So the number is right and the name is borrowed.
defectsNoCounterCanSee.whyItMatters: A later reader who takes the module's definition at face value - and the module is now the authority the builder imports - will read 607 as 607 glyphs drawn by flattened widget appearances in a file that has none. No counter can see a key name meaning two things.
defectsNoCounterCanSee.notScored: This is a report-semantics hazard, not a packet defect. Recorded, not edited.

defectsNoCounterCanSee.title: The three canonical fixtures are one person convicted three times, and the shared sequence number is unfalsifiable from the record.
defectsNoCounterCanSee.what: All three canonical fixtures carry the same petitioner (Jordan Avery Reyes, born 1991-04-17), the same court (Marion Superior Court, Criminal Division), the same conviction date (2015-06-18) and cause numbers differing only in the case-type token: 49D01-1503-F6-011234, -F5-011234, -CM-011234. The three boundary fixtures share a persona the same way.
defectsNoCounterCanSee.myJudgement: The shared persona is the factory's fixture convention and is not a defect. On the shared sequence 011234 I withdraw the ground I gave last round. I argued then that 'a sequence number is what distinguishes one cause from another within a court and period' - but that sentence is itself an assertion of Indiana clerk practice, sourced to nothing in this repository or in mounted custody. It is precisely the kind of assertion I am about to say FIX04 was right to refuse about case-type tokens, and I cannot hold FIX04 to a standard I exempt myself from. Unfalsifiable from the record, therefore unscored.

judgementOnFix04sCauseNumberReasoning.theReasoningTested: FIX04 moved the d6 boundary SEQUENCE rather than the case-type token, on the ground that no Indiana conviction case-type token table exists in this repository or in mounted custody, that the one case type the held source publishes is XP - the type of the expungement case, not of the underlying conviction - and that FB therefore cannot be shown wrong and no replacement could be shown right without asserting clerk practice as record fact.
judgementOnFix04sCauseNumberReasoning.myVerdict: SOUND, and it is the right remedy. The sequence carries no charge-level claim, so moving it discharges the collision and asserts nothing new. Moving the token would have required this factory to assert an Indiana charging convention it cannot source.
judgementOnFix04sCauseNumberReasoning.iTestedTheNegativeClaimRatherThanAccepti: I searched the mounted Indiana custody directly. The held legal review publishes XP under Administrative Rule 8(B)(3) and, at line 178, MC for a matter with no cause number assigned. So the held source publishes TWO case types, not one - FIX04's supporting sentence is off by one. Neither is a conviction case-type token, so the conclusion is unaffected and the reasoning stands. I record the correction because the sentence is stated as a fact about custody.
judgementOnFix04sCauseNumberReasoning.andICorrectMyOwnPriorRow: My last row asserted that 'FB is bound inside this repository to Class B'. It is not bound by anything except three builder scripts agreeing with each other - my own prior row conceded exactly that, calling the token table 'the builder agreeing with itself, not independent evidence', and it is self-contradicting, since d6 boundary pairs FB with Class D. FIX04 is right that the token/offence-level pairing is unsettled and right to leave it unscored.
judgementOnFix04sCauseNumberReasoning.whatMattersIsThatTheDecisiveGroundIsDisc: My decisive ground was never the token table. It was that one string was asserted as the cause number of two different convictions. d6 boundary is now ...654321 and felony boundary ...123456. Distinct. Discharged.

judgementOnTheDeclinedSharedSequence.whatFix04Declined: It declined to change the shared canonical sequence 49D01-1503-{F6,F5,CM}-011234, on the ground that the three are distinct strings, so VF30's decisive ground - one string asserted of two convictions - does not obtain.
judgementOnTheDeclinedSharedSequence.myVerdict: CORRECT, and correct on a stronger ground than the one FIX04 gave. The three strings are indeed distinct, so the collision ground does not reach them. But the ground I would have needed to fail them - that a sequence number cannot recur across case types in one court and period - is an assertion of clerk practice with no source in this repository or in mounted custody. It is the same category of claim that disqualifies the token argument. Having asked FIX04 to hold that line, I hold it too. Unscored.
